long_biography.plain_text:
A crisis at DFS brought co-founder Robert Miller home from his honeymoon to confront a business that had expanded faster than its financial controls. He spent two years closing its military sales operations, collecting debts and fulfilling outstanding orders. Cash from airport shops, increasingly busy with Japanese travellers, helped meet those obligations and made travel retail the company's focus.

When his partners later sold their stakes to LVMH, Miller chose to retain his own substantial holding. His family encouraged that decision through the difficult years that followed. The earlier near-collapse taught him to put financial controls and experienced accounting staff at the centre of the business.
